# Oakfield Bridge

Oakfield Bridge is a steel truss bridge over the Ash River. It opened in 1932, replaced a ferry that had run since 1870, and now carries about 40,000 vehicles a day.

The county rebuilt the deck in 1988 after inspectors found corrosion in the stringers. Traffic ran on one lane for eleven months. Local shops on the east bank lost a lot of trade that year, and two closed.

A second crossing has been proposed three times. Each time it lost the vote, mostly over cost. The current estimate is $310 million.

## Visiting

There's a footpath on the north side. Parking is free on weekends at the east end, near the old ferry landing.
